# [ShadowClaw](https://xt-ml.github.io/shadow-claw/)

> A dual-runtime AI assistant featuring both a rich, client-side browser orchestrator (reasoning, state machine, dynamic context windowing, and tool execution running off the main thread in a Web Worker in the browser or Electron) and a host-native headless server agent (`shadow-claw agent`). Instantly launchable via `npx shadow-claw dev --open`, driven by a full-featured CLI, and backed by a 24/7 Node.js service layer (control plane, task scheduler, proxying, and MCP).

## Quick Start & CLI

Run instantly without cloning the repo:

- `npx shadow-claw dev --open` — Start local services and launch the assistant in your browser immediately.
- `npx shadow-claw agent run "prompt"` — Run autonomous headless agent prompts directly on the server or host CLI (backed by SQLite, host OS tools, and streaming stdout).
- `npx shadow-claw agent model list` — List local cached ONNX/GGUF models, context lengths, and active defaults.
- `npx shadow-claw agent model download [id]` — Pre-download model weights from Hugging Face with an interactive terminal progress bar.
- `npx shadow-claw agent model set [id]` — Set the default model for headless CLI execution in workspace config.
- `npx shadow-claw agent tools` — Inspect available tools and execution environments.
- `npx shadow-claw agent tool <name> [jsonArgs]` — Execute any tool directly from the terminal without model invocation.
- `npx shadow-claw agent skill <name>` — Execute a declarative skill tool chain.
- `npx shadow-claw agent import <url> [options]` — Discover and import remote RFC v0.2.0 skills, declarative tools, and companion scripts directly into the agent workspace.
- `npx shadow-claw agent listen` — Start a headless agent listener over WebRTC to accept peer prompts, run the orchestration loop, and receive files.
- `npx shadow-claw agent init <dir>` — Scaffold a headless agent workspace with interactive model selection and prewarming.
- `npx shadow-claw init <dir>` — Scaffold a custom template or knowledge hub.
- `npx shadow-claw server` — Run headless 24/7 backend services (task scheduler, MCP, REST API).
- `npx shadow-claw server --a2a` — Expose the A2A v1.0 agent card, JSON-RPC, and SSE endpoints.
- `npx shadow-claw send "prompt"` — Dispatch prompts to connected clients or peer agents directly from your terminal (supports -f, --file).
- `npx shadow-claw send-file <file> --client <peerId>` — Transfer files directly to connected peers over WebRTC with optional prompt instructions.
- `npx shadow-claw mcp [--workspace <dir>]` — Run the official Stateless Model Context Protocol (2026-07-28) server over STDIO or HTTP, exposing host-native CLI agent tools (`read_file`, `write_file`, `bash`, `git_*`) and server control plane tools with tri-tier naming and sandbox isolation.
- [CLI Reference](https://xt-ml.github.io/shadow-claw/docs/subsystems/cli.md) — Complete guide to all CLI commands, flags, and control plane options.

## When to Use This

ShadowClaw is best suited for:

- **Dual-runtime flexibility (browser UI + server CLI):** Seamlessly transition between an interactive web/Electron GUI (with visual A2UI components, chat, files, and tasks) and an autonomous headless agent running directly in terminal pipelines, CI/CD, or automated servers.
- **Client-side orchestration of the agentic loop:** When you want the entire agent decision loop—state machine, prompt assembly, dynamic context windowing, and tool dispatch—to execute client-side off the main thread in a browser Web Worker or Electron.
- **Host-native server CLI agent (`shadow-claw agent`):** Running autonomous agents directly in Node.js on bare-metal or container servers with host OS shell execution (`child_process`), direct filesystem handles (`NodeFsDirectoryHandle`), SQLite conversation storage, and out-of-the-box in-process Transformers.js ONNX execution (`onnx-community/gemma-3-1b-it-ONNX-GQA`), Llamafile binaries, or OpenRouter (`openrouter/free`).
- **Remote skill & declarative tool discovery:** Importing decentralized skills and tools from RFC v0.2.0 endpoints directly into browser OPFS or host CLI workspaces via `shadow-claw agent import` without writing custom glue code.
- **Direct tool & skill inspection:** Executing agent tools (`shadow-claw agent tool <name> '{"arg":"val"}'`) and declarative skill toolchains directly from scripts or shell pipelines without invoking model inference.
- **Zero-install instant launch & CLI driving:** Starting immediately with `npx shadow-claw dev --open`, scaffolding custom templates with `npx shadow-claw init`, or driving connected browser sessions, tasks, and backups through the `shadow-claw` CLI.
- **Ultra-safe sandboxed execution:** Running real code, bash, and system operations inside isolated client-side environments—including an in-browser WebVM (v86 Alpine Linux running in WASM inside a Web Worker), `just-bash` POSIX emulation, and sandboxed OPFS/IndexedDB storage.
- **Control plane & client bridge:** Driving browser and Electron execution surfaces from external tools, scripts, or CLI commands via real-time SSE, WebSockets, or WebRTC.
- **Peer-to-peer agent collaboration & file sharing:** Connecting multiple headless CLI agents and browser clients over WebRTC DataChannels, dispatching peer prompts, transferring files directly from the Files browser and File Viewer UI or terminal CLI (`send-file`, `send --file`), and allowing agents to autonomously discover and prompt peers via built-in tools (`prompt_peer`, `list_peers`, `send_file`).
- **Headless server & background services:** Running a persistent 24/7 Node backend (`shadow-claw server`) to manage client schedules in SQLite, tick cron schedules, wake dormant clients via Web Push, and serve REST APIs and MCP endpoints.
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations:** Interfacing with external coding agents (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Goose) via STDIO or Streamable HTTP, exposing host-native CLI agent tools against real workspace files with strict root traversal security, isolated bash execution, and tri-tier tool hierarchy.
- **Static knowledge hubs:** Authoring and deploying static documentation and agent-assisted knowledge repositories.

When to look elsewhere:

- Simple single-turn text completion scripts that do not require tool execution, agentic loops, reactive UI surfaces, or persistent multi-conversation storage.
